purpose: Validate the stock upstream VS1/F4 Virtual_WRITE transport without intentionally changing the effective controller value.

target.name: ordinary day room setpoint
target.write_policy: Read the current byte via VS1/F7, then write exactly that same byte via stock upstream VS1/F4.

checks: Require splitter active/running and normal vs1protocol=False baseline.
Stop Party if active and stop splitter for exclusive serial ownership.
Require pinned stock optolinkvs1.py Git blob.
Initialize VS1 and verify 00F8 identity is 20C2.
Write the identical byte via stock optolinkvs1.write_datapoint_ext/F4.
Read 0x2306 via F7 and require unchanged value.
Perform an additional final F7 verification.
Switch back to P300 directly and verify 00F8/2 = 20C2 before closing serial.
Restore splitter and Party service state.
interpretation: PASS validates the stock VS1/F4 transport handshake and same-value readback on this appliance. A separate value-changing +/-1 C test is still required before claiming that F4 state mutation is fully validated.

conclusion: The stock upstream VS1/F4 transport is accepted on this exact VDensHO1/20C2 appliance for an idempotent one-byte write to ordinary setpoint 0x2306.
The one-byte F4 response payload was 00; it is therefore not an echo of the written value.
A following F7 readback is required to verify the effective controller value.
This run does not yet prove that a changed value is applied; it proves transport/acknowledgement plus unchanged-value readback.
live_run.next_gate: Bounded 0x2306 value-changing test: baseline -> +/-1 C -> baseline, with F7 verification after both writes and P300 post-restore verification.
